## Why it made the list

Asking ¥21,990,000 (about €125,400). A two-storey wooden house finished in January 2015 in Yakumo-cho Hiyoshi, a quiet residential area in the green hills south of Matsue, the castle city of Shimane. 96 m² with a bright living, dining and kitchen room of about 20 tatami under a double-height ceiling, a modern fitted kitchen, a bathroom with a window and three bedrooms upstairs, on a 168 m² freehold plot with a lawn garden and parking for three cars. The house is empty and sold directly by the owning company, which is refreshing it now. JR Iya station is 7.2 km away.

## What it costs to buy this home

Buying in Japan adds about 6-9% in taxes and fees on top of the price: roughly €7,524 to €11,286 here, so plan for about €132,924 to €136,686 in total.

The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

Every year: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

General information, not tax advice: ask a local lawyer or notary for the exact figure.
